prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the vertical and radial layout from the upward-tilted head camera, with the wearer's nose and forehead brightest at the bottom center (0.05–0.15 m), their red-shirted torso just beyond (0.2–0.5 m), the curved overhead wall/ceiling at mid-range above (0.5–1.0 m), and the wooden scaffolding floor receding below into the dark background (1.5–3.0 m). It shows the clipboard in the wearer's hand on the left of the frame (0.4–0.6 m), the wearer's other arm reaching up to touch the overhead surface with a spray can within arm's reach in frames 1–2 (0.6–0.8 m) before retracting to chest level in frames 3–5 (0.4–0.5 m), and a coworker in a high-visibility vest standing on the scaffolding 1.2–2.5 m away to the left of the frame (1.0–2.0 m from the wearer's torso), facing parallel to the wall and looking away from the camera wearer. Across the five frames, the depth gradients track the wearer rotating in frame 4—where the overhead wall shifts to the upper right and becomes very bright (0.3–0.5 m)—and turning back in frame 5 as the partially cut-off coworker on the left edge moves slightly closer (~1.2 m) while occluding the scaffolding planks behind them. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the steep vertical drop between the wearer's torso, the coworker's lower body, and the underlying scaffolding planks immediately apparent despite the wide-angle distortion. However, it is unreliable on the smooth, featureless overhead ceiling (especially in frame 4 where illumination causes over-saturated near-depth values) and flattens the coworker's legs into the surrounding scaffolding depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground silhouettes of the camera wearer's own body (0.05–0.8 m away at the bottom-center and right), the held clipboard on the left side of the torso (0.4–0.6 m, within arm's reach), and the second person standing to the left on the scaffolding below (1.2–2.5 m away from the wearer and ~1.0–1.5 m from the clipboard), while leaving the overhead ceiling, ducting, and scaffolding planks unsegmented in black. Across the five frames, the wearer's mask tracks their extended right-side arm reaching upward in frames 1–2, lowering in frame 3, and bringing the spray can down near the torso in frames 4–5 as the wearer turns away and back, while the coworker on the left edge remains partially out of view, oriented sideways relative to the wearer, and looking away. The masks clearly delineate the boundary and partial occlusion where the clipboard overlaps the wearer's chest and left hand, as well as the separation between the wearer's forearm and the nearby coworker in frames 1 and 5, which can blend into the cluttered scaffolding background in RGB. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the clipboard as an 'umbrella' in frames 1–2, a 'person' in frame 3, and a 'book' in frame 4 before missing it in frame 5. It also mislabels the coworker in the high-visibility vest as an 'airplane' in frame 3, misses them entirely in frame 4 when they shift to the top-left corner, and splits them into 'horse' and 'person' masks in frame 5 while failing to segment the held spray can.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D yellow body keypoints and torso/arm links only in frames 1–3, localized on the camera wearer's own head at the bottom center (0.05–0.15 m), shoulders/chest (0.2–0.5 m), and raised arm on the right side of the frame (0.5–0.8 m), while failing to detect the coworker standing 1.2–2.5 m away on the left. In frames 1–2, the skeleton outlines the wearer's torso and the extended arm reaching upward within arm's reach of the overhead surface while the other arm holding the clipboard (~0.5 m away on the left) is only partially represented; in frame 3, the right-side arm link drops lower as the wearer retracts their arm and rotates slightly. No magenta hand skeletons are detected in any frame, even though both of the wearer's gloved hands (holding the clipboard on the left and the spray can on the right) are within 0.4–0.8 m in the foreground. While the skeleton links in frames 1–3 help abstract the geometric angle of the wearer's shoulder and raised upper arm through the loose fabric of the red sweatshirt, the map is severely unreliable overall. Because of the extreme top-down egocentric viewpoint and heavy self-occlusion at the frame edges, it places noisy facial keypoints across the wearer's chin, misses the coworker (who faces away/sideways on the left edge) in all frames, and completely loses all body and hand detections in frames 4 and 5.
